sanskrit: punaḥ suptān upādhākṣīd bālakān vāraṇāvate śayānān āryayā sārdhaṃ ko nu tat kartum arhati
english: Again he set fire to the sleeping boys at Vāraṇāvata, lying there with their noble mother — who indeed could deserve to do such a thing?

sanskrit: yatrāryā rudatī bhītā pāṇḍavān idam abravīt mahad vyasanam āpannā śikhinā parivāritā
english: There the noble woman, weeping and terrified, surrounded by fire, caught in great calamity, spoke thus to the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: hā hatāsmi kuto nv adya bhavec chāntir ihānalāt anāthā vinaśiṣyāmi bālakaiḥ putrakaiḥ saha
english: "Alas, I am slain! Where now can there be escape from this fire? Helpless, I will perish along with these boys, these little children."

sanskrit: tatra bhīmo mahābāhur vāyuvegaparākramaḥ āryām āśvāsayām āsa bhrātṝṃś cāpi vṛkodaraḥ
english: Then mighty-armed Bhīma, Vṛkodara, whose prowess was swift as the wind, reassured the noble woman and his brothers as well.

sanskrit: vainateyo yathā pakṣī garuḍaḥ patatāṃ varaḥ tathaivābhipatiṣyāmi bhayaṃ vo neha vidyate
english: "As Garuḍa, son of Vinatā, best of birds, soars swiftly, so shall I carry you all — have no fear here."

sanskrit: āryām aṅkena vāmena rājānaṃ dakṣiṇena ca aṃsayoś ca yamau kṛtvā pṛṣṭhe bībhatsum eva ca
english: He took the noble woman on his left hip, the king on his right, placed the twin brothers on his shoulders, and Bībhatsu on his back.

sanskrit: sahasotpatya vegena sarvān ādāya vīryavān bhrātṝn āryāṃ ca balavān mokṣayām āsa pāvakāt
english: Leaping up with great speed, that powerful and valiant man, taking all his brothers and the noble woman, rescued them from the fire.

sanskrit: te rātrau prasthitāḥ sarve mātrā saha yaśasvinaḥ abhyagacchan mahāraṇyaṃ hiḍimbavanam antikāt
english: Those illustrious ones set out by night, all together with their mother, and came near to the great forest, the forest of Hiḍimba.

sanskrit: śrāntāḥ prasuptās tatreme mātrā saha suduḥkhitāḥ suptāṃś cainān abhyagacchad dhiḍimbā nāma rākṣasī
english: Exhausted and deeply sorrowful, they slept there with their mother. And while they slept, a rākṣasī named Hiḍimbā came upon them.

sanskrit: bhīmasya pādau kṛtvā tu sva utsaṅge tato balāt paryamardata saṃhṛṣṭā kalyāṇī mṛdupāṇinā
english: She placed Bhīma's feet in her own lap and, delighted, gently stroked them with her soft hands.

sanskrit: tām abudhyad ameyātmā balavān satyavikramaḥ paryapṛcchac ca tāṃ bhīmaḥ kim ihecchasy anindite
english: The mighty one of immeasurable soul, true in valor, Bhīma awoke and questioned her: "What do you desire here, O blameless one?"

sanskrit: tayoḥ śrutvā tu kathitam āgacchad rākṣasādhamaḥ bhīmarūpo mahānādān visṛjan bhīmadarśanaḥ
english: Hearing what had passed between the two, that vilest of rākṣasas came forward, terrible in form, emitting great roars, dreadful in appearance.

sanskrit: kena sārdhaṃ kathayasi ānayainaṃ mamāntikam hiḍimbe bhakṣayiṣyāvo na ciraṃ kartum arhasi
english: "With whom do you speak? Bring him to me! Hiḍimbā, we shall eat him — do not delay in doing this."

sanskrit: sā kṛpāsaṃgṛhītena hṛdayena manasvinī nainam aicchat tadākhyātum anukrośād aninditā
english: But she, that blameless high-minded woman, with a heart seized by compassion and moved by pity, did not wish to betray him.

sanskrit: sa nādān vinadan ghorān rākṣasaḥ puruṣādakaḥ abhyadravata vegena bhīmasenaṃ tadā kila
english: Then that man-eating rākṣasa, uttering fearful roars, charged at full speed toward Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: tam abhidrutya saṃkruddho vegena mahatā balī agṛhṇāt pāṇinā pāṇiṃ bhīmasenasya rākṣasaḥ
english: Rushing at him in great fury and with tremendous speed, that powerful rākṣasa seized Bhīmasena's hand in his own hand.

sanskrit: indrāśanisamasparśaṃ vajrasaṃhananaṃ dṛḍham saṃhatya bhīmasenāya vyākṣipat sahasā karam
english: That hand, firm as Indra's thunderbolt and hard as a vajra to the touch, he suddenly flung back at Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: gṛhītaṃ pāṇinā pāṇiṃ bhīmaseno 'tha rakṣasā nāmṛṣyata mahābāhus tatrākrudhyad vṛkodaraḥ
english: Mighty-armed Bhīmasena, Vṛkodara, did not tolerate having his hand seized by the rākṣasa — there he blazed with anger.

sanskrit: tatrāsīt tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ bhīmasenahiḍimbayoḥ sarvāstraviduṣor ghoraṃ vṛtravāsavayor iva
english: There was a tumultuous and terrible battle between Bhīmasena and Hiḍimba, both versed in all weapons, like the combat between Vṛtra and Vāsava.

sanskrit: hatvā hiḍimbaṃ bhīmo 'tha prasthito bhrātṛbhiḥ saha hiḍimbām agrataḥ kṛtvā yasyāṃ jāto ghaṭotkacaḥ
english: Having slain Hiḍimba, Bhīma then set forth with his brothers, placing Hiḍimbā ahead of them — she by whom Ghaṭotkaca was born.

sanskrit: tataś ca prādravan sarve saha mātrā yaśasvinaḥ ekacakrām abhimukhāḥ saṃvṛtā brāhmaṇavrajaiḥ
english: Then all of those illustrious ones ran forward together with their mother, heading toward Ekacakrā, accompanied by bands of brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: prasthāne vyāsa eṣāṃ ca mantrī priyahito 'bhavat tato 'gacchann ekacakrāṃ pāṇḍavāḥ saṃśitavratāḥ
english: In their departure Vyāsa served as a counselor, dear and beneficial to them; and so the Pāṇḍavas, firm in their vows, went to Ekacakrā.

sanskrit: tatrāpy āsādayām āsur bakaṃ nāma mahābalam puruṣādaṃ pratibhayaṃ hiḍimbenaiva saṃmitam
english: There too they encountered a supremely powerful man-eater named Baka, terrifying in might, the equal of Hiḍimba.

sanskrit: taṃ cāpi vinihatyograṃ bhīmaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ sahito bhrātṛbhiḥ sarvair drupadasya puraṃ yayau
english: Bhīma, best among those who strike, slew that fierce one as well, and then went with all his brothers to the city of Drupada.

sanskrit: labdhāham api tatraiva vasatā savyasācinā yathā tvayā jitā kṛṣṇa rukmiṇī bhīṣmakātmajā
english: And it was there that I was won by Savyasācin — even as you, O Kṛṣṇa, won Rukmiṇī, daughter of Bhīṣmaka.

sanskrit: evaṃ suyuddhe pārthena jitāhaṃ madhusūdana svayaṃvare mahat karma kṛtvā nasukaraṃ paraiḥ
english: Thus was I won by Pārtha in glorious combat, O Madhusūdana, at the svayaṃvara, performing a great feat impossible for others.

sanskrit: evaṃ kleśaiḥ subahubhiḥ kliśyamānāḥ suduḥkhitāḥ nivasāmāryayā hīnāḥ kṛṣṇa dhaumyapuraḥsarāḥ
english: Thus afflicted by very many hardships, deeply sorrowful, bereft of our noble mother-in-law, O Kṛṣṇa, we dwell here with Dhaumya leading us.

sanskrit: ta ime siṃhavikrāntā vīryeṇābhyadhikāḥ paraiḥ vihīnaiḥ parikliśyantīṃ samupekṣanta māṃ katham
english: How could those lion-striding men, superior to their enemies in valor, look on while I, bereft, suffer — how could they endure it?

sanskrit: etādṛśāni duḥkhāni sahante durbalīyasām dīrghakālaṃ pradīptāni pāpānāṃ kṣudrakarmaṇām
english: Such sorrows, blazing long, are endured only by the weak, by sinners of base deeds.

sanskrit: kule mahati jātāsmi divyena vidhinā kila pāṇḍavānāṃ priyā bhāryā snuṣā pāṇḍor mahātmanaḥ
english: I was born into a great lineage, and by divine ordinance became the beloved wife of the Pāṇḍavas, daughter-in-law of the great-souled Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: kacagraham anuprāptā sāsmi kṛṣṇa varā satī pañcānām indrakalpānāṃ prekṣatāṃ madhusūdana
english: Yet I, O Kṛṣṇa, that excellent and virtuous woman, was seized by the hair while those five, the equals of Indra, looked on — O Madhusūdana!

sanskrit: ity uktvā prārudat kṛṣṇā mukhaṃ pracchādya pāṇinā padmakośaprakāśena mṛdunā mṛdubhāṣiṇī
english: Having spoken thus, Kṛṣṇā wept, covering her face with her hand — that soft hand, bright as a lotus bud — she who speaks softly.

sanskrit: stanāv apatitau pīnau sujātau śubhalakṣaṇau abhyavarṣata pāñcālī duḥkhajair aśrubindubhiḥ
english: The Pāñcālī drenched her two full, well-formed, auspiciously marked breasts with tears born of sorrow, falling down upon them.

sanskrit: cakṣuṣī parimārjantī niḥśvasantī punaḥ punaḥ bāṣpapūrṇena kaṇṭhena kruddhā vacanam abravīt
english: Wiping her eyes, sighing again and again, with a throat choked with tears, she spoke in anger.

sanskrit: naiva me patayaḥ santi na putrā madhusūdana na bhrātaro na ca pitā naiva tvaṃ na ca bāndhavāḥ
english: "I have no husbands, no sons, O Madhusūdana, no brothers, no father, not even you, no kinsmen —

sanskrit: ye māṃ viprakṛtāṃ kṣudrair upekṣadhvaṃ viśokavat na hi me śāmyate duḥkhaṃ karṇo yat prāhasat tadā
english: — you who look on carelessly while I am outraged by those vile men! My grief does not subside — the grief of that day when Karṇa laughed at me."

sanskrit: athainām abravīt kṛṣṇas tasmin vīrasamāgame rodiṣyanti striyo hy evaṃ yeṣāṃ kruddhāsi bhāmini
english: Then Kṛṣṇa spoke to her in that assembly of heroes: "The wives of those at whom you are angry, O beautiful one, shall weep thus in return."

sanskrit: bībhatsuśarasaṃchannāñ śoṇitaughapariplutān nihatāñ jīvitaṃ tyaktvā śayānān vasudhātale
english: "Slain, having given up their lives, drenched in floods of blood, covered with Bībhatsu's arrows, they shall lie on the surface of the earth."

sanskrit: yat samarthaṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ tat kariṣyāmi mā śucaḥ satyaṃ te pratijānāmi rājñāṃ rājñī bhaviṣyasi
english: "Whatever the Pāṇḍavas are capable of, that I will ensure — do not grieve. I promise you truly: you shall be the queen among queens."

sanskrit: pated dyaur himavāñ śīryet pṛthivī śakalībhavet śuṣyet toyanidhiḥ kṛṣṇe na me moghaṃ vaco bhavet
english: "Though the sky should fall, though the Himālaya crumble, though the earth shatter into pieces, though the ocean dry up — O Kṛṣṇā, my words shall not be in vain."

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumna uvāca ahaṃ droṇaṃ haniṣyāmi śikhaṇḍī tu pitāmaham duryodhanaṃ bhīmasenaḥ karṇaṃ hantā dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna spoke: "I shall slay Droṇa, Śikhaṇḍī shall slay the grandsire, Bhīmasena shall slay Duryodhana, and Dhanaṃjaya shall be the slayer of Karṇa."

sanskrit: rāmakṛṣṇau vyapāśritya ajeyāḥ sma śucismite api vṛtrahaṇā yuddhe kiṃ punar dhṛtarāṣṭrajaiḥ
english: "Supported by Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, we are unconquerable, O bright-smiling one — even against Vṛtra's slayer in battle, let alone the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity ukte 'bhimukhā vīrā vāsudevam upasthitā teṣāṃ madhye mahābāhuḥ keśavo vākyam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When this was spoken, the heroes turned toward Vāsudeva and stood before him; and mighty-armed Keśava spoke his word among them.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca nedaṃ kṛcchram anuprāpto bhavān syād vasudhādhipa yady ahaṃ dvārakāyāṃ syāṃ rājan saṃnihitaḥ purā
english: Vāsudeva said: "This hardship would not have come upon you, O lord of the earth, had I, O king, been present at Dvārakā earlier."

sanskrit: āgaccheyam ahaṃ dyūtam anāhūto 'pi kauravaiḥ āmbikeyena durdharṣa rājñā duryodhanena ca
english: "I would have come to that dice-game uninvited even by the Kauravas, even by the king son of Ambikā, even by Duryodhana, O unconquerable one."

sanskrit: vārayeyam ahaṃ dyūtaṃ bahūn doṣān pradarśayan bhīṣmadroṇau samānāyya kṛpaṃ bāhlīkam eva ca
english: "I would have stopped that dice-game, pointing out its many faults, summoning Bhīṣma and Droṇa, and Kṛpa and Bāhlīka as well."

sanskrit: vaicitravīryaṃ rājānam alaṃ dyūtena kaurava putrāṇāṃ tava rājendra tvannimittam iti prabho
english: "I would have addressed the son of Vicitravīrya thus: Enough of this dice-game, O Kaurava — do this for the sake of your sons, O king of kings, for your own sake, O lord."

sanskrit: tatra vakṣyāmy ahaṃ doṣān yair bhavān avaropitaḥ vīrasenasuto yaiś ca rājyāt prabhraṃśitaḥ purā
english: "There I would have declared those faults by which you were brought low, and by which the son of Vīrasena too was formerly stripped of his kingdom."

sanskrit: abhakṣitavināśaṃ ca devanena viśāṃ pate sātatyaṃ ca prasaṅgasya varṇayeyaṃ yathātatham
english: "And the ruin that comes without enjoyment through gambling, O lord of men, and the persistence of the addiction — all this I would have described truthfully."

sanskrit: striyo 'kṣā mṛgayā pānam etat kāmasamutthitam vyasanaṃ catuṣṭayaṃ proktaṃ yai rājan bhraśyate śriyaḥ
english: "Women, dice, hunting, drink — these four vices arising from desire are cited as those by which, O king, a man falls from prosperity."

sanskrit: tatra sarvatra vaktavyaṃ manyante śāstrakovidāḥ viśeṣataś ca vaktavyaṃ dyūte paśyanti tadvidaḥ
english: "Those skilled in the śāstras hold that one must speak out in all such matters; and those who know gambling specifically hold that one must especially speak out against dice."

sanskrit: ekāhnā dravyanāśo 'tra dhruvaṃ vyasanam eva ca abhuktanāśaś cārthānāṃ vākpāruṣyaṃ ca kevalam
english: "In gambling there is certain loss of wealth in a single day, and addiction; wealth is destroyed without being enjoyed, and only harsh words result."

sanskrit: etac cānyac ca kauravya prasaṅgi kaṭukodayam dyūte brūyāṃ mahābāho samāsādyāmbikāsutam
english: "All this and more, O Kaurava, with its bitter end born of addiction, I would have said about dice, O mighty-armed one, upon reaching the son of Ambikā."

sanskrit: evam ukto yadi mayā gṛhṇīyād vacanaṃ mama anāmayaṃ syād dharmasya kurūṇāṃ kurunandana
english: "If, thus addressed by me, he had accepted my counsel, it would have been well for the law among the Kurus, O joy of the Kurus."

sanskrit: na cet sa mama rājendra gṛhṇīyān madhuraṃ vacaḥ pathyaṃ ca bharataśreṣṭha nigṛhṇīyāṃ balena tam
english: "But if, O king of kings, O best of Bhāratas, he had not accepted my sweet and wholesome counsel, I would have restrained him by force."

sanskrit: athainān abhinīyaivaṃ suhṛdo nāma durhṛdaḥ sabhāsadaś ca tān sarvān bhedayeyaṃ durodarān
english: "And thereafter, having led them in this manner, those who are called friends but are really enemies, all those assembled in the hall — I would have sown discord among those evil gamblers."

sanskrit: asāṃnidhyaṃ tu kauravya mamānarteṣv abhūt tadā yenedaṃ vyasanaṃ prāptā bhavanto dyūtakāritam
english: "But my absence from the Ānārta country at that time, O Kaurava — that is what led to this calamity of the dice-game befalling you."

sanskrit: so 'ham etya kuruśreṣṭha dvārakāṃ pāṇḍunandana aśrauṣaṃ tvāṃ vyasaninaṃ yuyudhānād yathātatham
english: "Then I, O best of Kurus, O son of Pāṇḍu, returning to Dvārakā, heard from Yuyudhāna of your misfortune exactly as it had occurred."

sanskrit: śrutvaiva cāhaṃ rājendra paramodvignamānasaḥ tūrṇam abhyāgato 'smi tvāṃ draṣṭukāmo viśāṃ pate
english: "And having heard, O king of kings, my mind utterly distressed, I have come swiftly, O lord of men, wishing to see you."

sanskrit: aho kṛcchram anuprāptāḥ sarve sma bharatarṣabha ye vayaṃ tvāṃ vyasaninaṃ paśyāmaḥ saha sodaraiḥ
english: "Alas, all of us have fallen into hardship, O bull of the Bhāratas — we who see you in this affliction together with your brothers."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca asāṃnidhyaṃ kathaṃ kṛṣṇa tavāsīd vṛṣṇinandana kva cāsīd vipravāsas te kiṃ vākārṣīḥ pravāsakaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "How was it, O Kṛṣṇa, O joy of the Vṛṣṇis, that you were absent? Where were you dwelling away from home, and what did you do while abroad?"

sanskrit: kṛṣṇa uvāca śālvasya nagaraṃ saubhaṃ gato 'haṃ bharatarṣabha vinihantuṃ naraśreṣṭha tatra me śṛṇu kāraṇam
english: Kṛṣṇa said: "I had gone, O bull of the Bhāratas, O best of men, to destroy Saubha, the city of Śālva — hear from me the reason for that."

sanskrit: mahātejā mahābāhur yaḥ sa rājā mahāyaśāḥ damaghoṣātmajo vīraḥ śiśupālo mayā hataḥ
english: "That great-spirited, mighty-armed, greatly renowned king, the valiant son of Damaghoṣa — Śiśupāla — was slain by me."

sanskrit: yajñe te bharataśreṣṭha rājasūye 'rhaṇāṃ prati sa roṣavaśasaṃprāpto nāmṛṣyata durātmavān
english: "At your Rājasūya sacrifice, O best of Bhāratas, in the matter of the offering of honor, overcome by rage, that evil-souled one would not endure it."

sanskrit: śrutvā taṃ nihataṃ śālvas tīvraroṣasamanvitaḥ upāyād dvārakāṃ śūnyām ihasthe mayi bhārata
english: "Śālva, hearing of his slaying, filled with burning rage, marched against Dvārakā while it was empty, O Bhārata, while I was here."

sanskrit: sa tatra yodhito rājan bālakair vṛṣṇipuṃgavaiḥ āgataḥ kāmagaṃ saubham āruhyaiva nṛśaṃsakṛt
english: "He was fought there, O king, by young champions of the Vṛṣṇi clan; that doer of cruel deeds came aboard his wish-flying city Saubha."

sanskrit: tato vṛṣṇipravīrāṃs tān bālān hatvā bahūṃs tadā purodyānāni sarvāṇi bhedayām āsa durmatiḥ
english: "Then that wicked one, having slain many of those young Vṛṣṇi champions, proceeded to shatter all the city's parks and gardens."

sanskrit: uktavāṃś ca mahābāho kvāsau vṛṣṇikulādhamaḥ vāsudevaḥ sumandātmā vasudevasuto gataḥ
english: "And he declared aloud, O mighty-armed one: 'Where has that wretch of the Vṛṣṇi clan gone? Where is Vāsudeva, that feeble-minded son of Vasudeva?'"

sanskrit: tasya yuddhārthino darpaṃ yuddhe nāśayitāsmy aham ānartāḥ satyam ākhyāta tatra gantāsmi yatra saḥ
english: "'I shall destroy in battle the arrogance of that seeker of combat. O Ānārtas, tell me truly where he is — I shall go there.'"

sanskrit: taṃ hatvā vinivartiṣye kaṃsakeśiniṣūdanam ahatvā na nivartiṣye satyenāyudham ālabhe
english: "'Having slain him, I shall return — I who slew Kaṃsa and Keśin. Without slaying him I shall not return — I swear by my weapons in truth.'"

sanskrit: kvāsau kvāsāv iti punas tatra tatra vidhāvati mayā kila raṇe yuddhaṃ kāṅkṣamāṇaḥ sa saubharāṭ
english: "'Where is he, where is he?' — crying thus, he ran here and there; that king of Saubha was indeed seeking battle with me in combat."

sanskrit: adya taṃ pāpakarmāṇaṃ kṣudraṃ viśvāsaghātinam śiśupālavadhāmarṣād gamayiṣye yamakṣayam
english: "'Today I shall send that sinful, vile, treacherous one — enraged over the slaying of Śiśupāla — to the realm of death.'"

sanskrit: mama pāpasvabhāvena bhrātā yena nipātitaḥ śiśupālo mahīpālas taṃ vadhiṣye mahītale
english: "'He by whose sinful nature my kinsman, Śiśupāla, king of the earth, was struck down — him I shall slay upon this earth.'"

sanskrit: bhrātā bālaś ca rājā ca na ca saṃgrāmamūrdhani pramattaś ca hato vīras taṃ haniṣye janārdanam
english: "'A kinsman, young, and a king at that — not slain at the forefront of battle but killed off-guard, a hero — I will slay that Janārdana.'"

sanskrit: evamādi mahārāja vilapya divam āsthitaḥ kāmagena sa saubhena kṣiptvā māṃ kurunandana
english: "Lamenting in these and other words, O great king, he mounted to the sky in that wish-flying Saubha and hurled abuse at me, O joy of the Kurus."

sanskrit: tam aśrauṣam ahaṃ gatvā yathā vṛttaḥ sudurmatiḥ mayi kauravya duṣṭātmā mārttikāvatako nṛpaḥ
english: "Upon returning, I heard how that very wicked one had behaved toward me, O Kaurava — that corrupt-souled king, the lord of Mārtikāvata."

sanskrit: tato 'ham api kauravya roṣavyākulalocanaḥ niścitya manasā rājan vadhāyāsya mano dadhe
english: "Then I too, O Kaurava, my eyes disturbed with rage, made up my mind firmly, O king, and set my heart on his destruction."

sanskrit: ānarteṣu vimardaṃ ca kṣepaṃ cātmani kaurava pravṛddham avalepaṃ ca tasya duṣkṛtakarmaṇaḥ
english: "The trampling of the Ānārta people, the insults against me personally, O Kaurava, and the swollen arrogance of that evil-deeded one —"

sanskrit: tataḥ saubhavadhāyāhaṃ pratasthe pṛthivīpate sa mayā sāgarāvarte dṛṣṭa āsīt parīpsatā
english: "— and so, O lord of the earth, I set out for the destruction of Saubha. He was sighted by me in a whirlpool of the ocean, as I sought him."

sanskrit: tataḥ pradhmāpya jalajaṃ pāñcajanyam ahaṃ nṛpa āhūya śālvaṃ samare yuddhāya samavasthitaḥ
english: "Then, O king, I sounded the conch Pāñcajanya, born of the waters, and calling out Śālva, I took my stand ready for battle in the combat."
